signals.title: FDA expanded its 2026 yellow-oleander supplement warning
signals.takeaway: FDA added another product to its warning about supplements sold as tejocote root or Brazil seed that were found to contain toxic yellow oleander instead of the labeled ingredient.
signals.whyItMatters: Botanica should treat identity testing and adulteration screening as a first-class gate, especially for folkloric weight-loss or cross-border botanical supply lanes.

signals.title: FTC's substantiation bar still applies across every health-adjacent channel
signals.takeaway: FTC continues to frame health-product marketing around truthful, non-misleading claims backed by competent and reliable scientific evidence, including implied claims across ads, packaging, social, PR, and influencer activity.
signals.whyItMatters: Botanica can explore bold states internally, but public copy has to stay materially narrower than the R&D imagination and cannot rely on vibes, testimonials, or implication tricks.

signals.title: FDA still places the supplement safety and labeling burden on the marketer
signals.takeaway: FDA reiterates that supplement manufacturers and distributors must ensure products are not adulterated or misbranded before marketing, with FDA acting post-market through enforcement, warnings, and recalls.
signals.whyItMatters: Every Botanica concept needs a launch gate covering identity, contaminants, claims, and label review before anything leaves internal R&D.

signals.title: NCCIH keeps ashwagandha in the useful-but-not-carefree bucket
signals.takeaway: NCCIH continues to flag rare liver-injury cases, pregnancy and breastfeeding exclusions, thyroid and autoimmune cautions, surgery concerns, and interactions with sedatives, anticonvulsants, immunosuppressants, diabetes medications, blood-pressure medications, and thyroid hormone.
signals.whyItMatters: Ashwagandha remains commercially attractive, but Botanica should never treat it as a frictionless hero ingredient and should keep explicit exclusion flags attached to every concept.

signals.title: Kava remains high-interest and high-caution
signals.takeaway: NCCIH still highlights rare but serious liver-injury cases, sedation overlap with alcohol or benzodiazepines, and pregnancy or breastfeeding concerns, along with cultivar and quality uncertainty.
signals.whyItMatters: Kava can stay on the board for sensory-rich evening concepts, but only as specialist-review-only and never as a casual mainstream calm product.

signals.title: Saffron remains Botanica's strongest evidence-led mood-tone lane
signals.takeaway: A 2026 GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of 34 randomized controlled trials keeps saffron near the top of the board for adult mood-related outcomes, while still requiring careful non-disease framing.
signals.whyItMatters: If Botanica wants one evidence-forward emotional-tone lead, saffron still looks cleaner and more defensible than many neighboring botanicals.

signals.title: 2026 evidence still supports adaptogen interest, but not lazy certainty
signals.takeaway: New 2026 reviews keep ashwagandha and rhodiola relevant for stress-resilience and psychometric outcomes, but emphasize heterogeneity, short study duration, and the need for cleaner long-term data.
signals.whyItMatters: This supports continued internal concepting for calm-focus and resilience products, but not inflated certainty, stimulant analog framing, or underplayed safety language.

signals.title: SPINS-style trade coverage still points to ashwagandha and alternative formats as live retail signals
signals.takeaway: Trade coverage of SPINS' 2026 ingredients-to-watch list keeps ashwagandha prominent while related coverage points to broader adoption across alternative dosage forms and adjacent mind-body positioning.
signals.whyItMatters: The white space is not another generic capsule; it's differentiated format, sensory identity, and tighter safety-reviewed positioning around felt experience rather than loud claims.

remedies.name: Golden Hour
remedies.promise: An internal R&D concept for warm, brighter emotional tone with a cleaner evidence anchor than most mood-lane botanicals.
remedies.evidence: Saffron remains the strongest evidence-led herb on this board thanks to the 2026 meta-analysis base; the supporting herbs are there to shape feel and ritual, not to carry claims.
remedies.risk: Keep antidepressant-adjacent framing, pregnancy screening, and interaction review in scope; no disorder, diagnosis, or dosing language.

remedies.name: Dawn Circuit
remedies.promise: A steadier focus concept aimed at clear-headed momentum rather than stimulant mimicry.
remedies.evidence: The adaptogen literature keeps rhodiola plausible but not certain, while lion's mane remains mixed and theanine helps hold the experience in a more conservative lane.
remedies.risk: Avoid ADHD, stimulant, prescription-drug analog, or productivity-overpromise language; keep rhodiola interaction review attached.

remedies.name: Soft Landing
remedies.promise: A lower-risk evening ritual lane with more room for sensory format differentiation than a kava-first concept.
remedies.evidence: Evidence is ingredient-specific and moderate at best, but the compliance posture is cleaner and the experience model is easier to frame conservatively.
remedies.risk: Sedation, pregnancy, and medication-interaction screening still apply; no sleep-cure or guaranteed next-day-performance language.

remedies.name: Neural Ember
remedies.promise: A bolder social-warmth hypothesis that could feel distinct if the serotonergic risk profile is handled with discipline.
remedies.evidence: Saffron is the evidence anchor; kanna is the differentiator and remains the weaker, more experimental link.
remedies.risk: Serotonergic, psychiatric, pregnancy, and interaction review required; specialist-review-only until a cleaner evidence and safety memo exists.

remedies.name: Desert Current
remedies.promise: A less-generic vitality lane that leans on traditional-system intrigue and broad performance-adjacent positioning without stimulant energy tropes.
remedies.evidence: Still exploratory and more interesting than proven; it needs tighter ingredient-by-ingredient evidence grading before it graduates.
remedies.risk: Hormone, blood-pressure, CYP, medication, and performance-claim review required.

remedies.name: Velvet Lantern
remedies.promise: A high-intensity ritual concept with obvious felt appeal, kept strictly in the internal sandbox for now.
remedies.evidence: The demand signal is real, but NCCIH safety language keeps the risk profile elevated and sourcing questions unresolved.
remedies.risk: Liver-risk, sedative/alcohol overlap, pregnancy exclusion, and quality-control review make this specialist-review-only.
